project.name: grok
project.commit_note: The staged checkout under `gt_results/arvo_385773651/_work/src/grok` is newer than the metadata vulnerable commit, but at the traced sites it still contains the pre-fix `ResIncludeBuffers` / `IncludeTracker` implementation shown in `patch.diff`. This GT is grounded in that staged vulnerable source.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 385773651 (grok): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target grk_decompress_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/385773651
bug_description.normalized: The staged 138-byte witness is a raw JPEG 2000 codestream whose SIZ marker sets `Xsiz=0x00002020`, `Ysiz=0x20202020`, `X0siz=0x00000320`, `Y0siz=0x00022020`, `XTsiz=0x20202020`, `YTsiz=0x20002020`, `XT0siz=0x00000020`, `YT0siz=0x00002020`, and `Csiz=4`, and whose component descriptors make component 0 use subsampling `(dx,dy)=(32,1)` while components 1-3 use `(32,32)`. The COD payload `00002020000000002000` selects LRCP with one resolution and no custom precinct sizes, so each component inherits the default precinct exponents `(15,15)`. The 7-byte POC payload `00002020202000` appends one extra LRCP progression, which makes `PacketIter::init` set `singleProgression_ = false` and forces `update_include()` down the vulnerable include-tracker path. `PacketManager::getParams` then derives `numPrecinctsPerRes[0] = 16381` from the attacker-controlled geometry. `IncludeTracker::get_include` uses that value and `numcomps = 4` to compute `len = 16381 * 4 + 7 = 65531`, then calls `ResIncludeBuffers::get_byte(resno, 65530)`. `get_byte` allocates a single 1024-byte chunk for `byteIndex = 8191`, returns `chunks[7] + 1023` (the last byte of that chunk), and `IncludeTracker::update` later treats that pointer as a buffer base. On the same added LRCP progression, the ninth packet visit reaches `compno = 0`, `resno = 0`, `layno = 0`, `precinctIndex = 8`, so `include_index = (0 * 16381 + 8) >> 3 = 1`; `uint8_t val = include[1]` reads one byte past the chunk and matches the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read at `PacketIter.h:131`. The patch text removes the `get_include()->get_byte()` pointer-returning path in favor of chunk-local update logic, which is the missing obligation this trace identifies, but Stage 02 did not perform fixed-version dynamic validation.

source.value_from: In the saved 138-byte `poc` (sha256 `50baab0917cc0cec5d5ab803767eba14946fa691dee108dd0203139bbd75a561`), the SIZ payload after `FF51 0032` encodes `Xsiz=0x00002020`, `Ysiz=0x20202020`, `X0siz=0x00000320`, `Y0siz=0x00022020`, `XTsiz=0x20202020`, `YTsiz=0x20002020`, `XT0siz=0x00000020`, `YT0siz=0x00002020`, and `Csiz=4`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: Derived attacker-controlled precinct count later used as `numprecs` inside `IncludeTracker::get_include()` and `IncludeTracker::update()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: For component 0 / resolution 0, the staged geometry and subsampling produce `precinctGridWidth = 1`, `precinctGridHeight = 16381`, and `num_precincts = 16381`; components 1-3 each produce only 513 precincts, so the stored maximum for `numPrecinctsPerRes[0]` remains 16381.

root_cause.description: The helper returns a pointer to one specific byte inside the lazily allocated 1024-byte chunk, but the caller later treats that interior pointer as the base of an addressable include buffer and indexes it with the global `include_index`.
root_cause.note: For the staged witness, step 9 calls `get_byte(resno, 65530)`, so this statement returns `chunks[7] + 1023`, i.e. the last byte of the only allocated chunk. The next packet whose `include_index` becomes `1` therefore dereferences one byte past that chunk.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `include` is the interior pointer returned by `get_include()`, but this statement indexes it as though it were a full buffer base.
sink.note: On the ninth packet visit of the added LRCP progression, `index = 0 * 16381 + 8 = 8`, so `include_index = 1`; because `include` already points to `chunks[7] + 1023`, `include[1]` reads the first byte beyond the 1024-byte allocation. The saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this exact line, and its allocation context points back to `ResIncludeBuffers::get_byte` line 81.

parser_admitted.description: By this loop, the witness has already passed codestream header parsing, accepted the crafted SIZ/COD/POC/SOT/SOD markers, and entered Tier-2 packet iteration on tile 0.
parser_admitted.note: The saved stack reaches `TileProcessor::decompressT2T1 -> T2Decompress::decompressPackets -> PacketIter::next_lrcp`, so the malformed codestream is admitted far enough to exercise the include-tracker logic before any packet payload parsing or later truncation handling stops execution.

fine_trace.note: The crafted SIZ marker is the first project-side source of the geometry that later sizes the include tracker. It sets `image->x1 = 8224`, `image->y1 = 0x20202020`, `image->x0 = 800`, `image->y0 = 0x22020`, `cp->t_width = 0x20202020`, `cp->t_height = 0x20002020`, `cp->tx0 = 32`, `cp->ty0 = 0x2020`, and `image->numcomps = 4`.

fine_trace.code:
grk_read<uint8_t>(headerData++, &tmp); /* SGcod (A) */
...
tcp->prg = (GRK_PROG_ORDER)tmp;
grk_read<uint16_t>(headerData, &tcp->num_layers_); /* SGcod (B) */
...
tcp->numLayersToDecompress = cp->coding_params_.dec_.layers_to_decompress_
                                ? cp->coding_params_.dec_.layers_to_decompress_
                                : tcp->num_layers_;
fine_trace.note: The COD payload `00002020000000002000` stores `tcp->csty = 0`, `tcp->prg = GRK_LRCP`, and `tcp->num_layers_ = 8224`. That establishes LRCP packet iteration and a large layer bound, but because `csty = 0` there are no custom precinct-size bytes in this marker.

The same COD marker turns `ndecomp = 0` into `tccp->numresolutions = 1`. Because `tccp->csty & J2K_CCP_CSTY_PRT` is false, the helper assigns the default precinct exponents `(15,15)` for resolution 0, and `read_cod` then copies those same settings to the other three components.

The POC payload `00002020202000` has exactly one 7-byte progression entry because `header_size = chunkSize = 7`. It appends `progressionOrderChange[1] = {res_s = 0, comp_s = 0, lay_e = 8224, res_e = 1, comp_e = 4, progression = GRK_LRCP}` and sets `tcp->numpocs = 1`, so packet processing now has two progressions instead of one.

PacketManager stores the SIZ-derived component count inside `IncludeTracker`. For this witness, the tracker is created with `numcomps = 4`, which later multiplies the per-resolution precinct count in `get_include()`.

Using the geometry from step 1, subsampling from step 2, and precinct exponents from step 4, component 0 / resolution 0 gets `tileCompBounds = [25,139296,257,536887360]`, `precinctGridWidth = 1`, `precinctGridHeight = 16381`, and `num_precincts = 16381`. Components 1-3 each compute only `1 * 513 = 513` precincts, so `updateNumPrecinctsPerRes(0, ...)` leaves the tracked maximum at `numPrecinctsPerRes[0] = 16381`.

depends_on.via: image->x1, image->y1, image->x0, image->y0, cp->t_width, cp->t_height, cp->tx0, cp->ty0

fine_trace.var: singleProgression_, numcomps, prog.progression, prog.lay_e, prog.res_e, prog.comp_e
fine_trace.note: For `pino = 1`, the extra POC entry from step 5 is selected. Because `packetManager->getNumProgressions() == 1` is false (`numpocs = 1`), `singleProgression_` stays false and `update_include()` will call the vulnerable include tracker instead of returning immediately. The active packet range for this iterator is LRCP over `layno < 8224`, `resno < 1`, and `compno < 4`.

On the crashing path `resno = 0`, so this helper reads `numprecs = 16381` from step 7 and `numcomps = 4` from step 6, computes `len = 65531`, and calls `get_byte(resno, 65530)` only to force allocation. That argument corresponds to the final tracked byte position, not to a chunk base.

With `index = 65530` from step 9, this code derives `byteIndex = 8191`, `chunkIndex = 7`, and `offset = 1023`. It allocates only `chunks[7]`, a single 1024-byte chunk, and returns `chunks[7] + 1023`, i.e. a pointer to the last byte inside that chunk.

On the active POC-added LRCP iterator from step 8, component 0 / resolution 0 has `prec_e = 16381`. The first eight visits to this block set bits 0..7 in the byte from step 10. On the ninth visit, `incrementInner` advances `precinctIndex` from 7 to 8, `8 < 16381` still holds, and `update_include()` is called again before any packet payload parsing changes control flow.

At the crashing visit, `compno = 0`, `precno = precinctIndex = 8`, and `numprecs = 16381`, so this statement computes `index = 8`, `include_index = 1`, and `shift = 0`. Because step 10 returned `include = chunks[7] + 1023`, `include[1]` dereferences address `chunks[7] + 1024`, which is exactly the first byte past the 1024-byte allocation reported by ASan.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run fed the staged 138-byte raw J2K `poc` (sha256 `50baab0917cc0cec5d5ab803767eba14946fa691dee108dd0203139bbd75a561`) to `grk_decompress_fuzzer`, which called `grk_decompress_read_header`, `grk_decompress_set_window`, and `grk_decompress`, and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `PacketIter.h:131`.

This GT does not claim that other codestreams sharing only the same SIZ/COD/POC header fields will also survive the first eight packet iterations and reach the ninth `PacketIter::next_lrcp` visit; Stage 01 preserved only this single crashing witness.
